The commit adds a new risk‑bearing claim (`history.high_recent_churn`) and updates related tests and UI text; the main thing to verify is that the backend actually provides this claim and that its inclusion does not break any downstream logic.

### What changed and why
* **`claimVocabulary.js`** – the constant `RISK_BEARING_CLAIM_IDS` now includes `"history.high_recent_churn"`.  
* **`claimVocabulary.test.js`** – a new test asserts that `isRiskBearingClaim` returns `true` for the new claim.  
* **`reviewTiers.js`** – the human‑readable description of `FILE_TIER_RULE` is expanded to mention the “high‑recent‑churn signal”.

commit_summary.message:
Treat history.high_recent_churn as risk-bearing

## Summary
- \`history.high_recent_churn\` (5+ changes to a file in the last 30 days) is already computed by the backend but was never included in the frontend's risk-bearing claim set, so it never affected file tiering.
- Added it to \`RISK_BEARING_CLAIM_IDS\` alongside the existing \`history.hot_file\`/\`history.first_author_touch\` signals, updated \`FILE_TIER_RULE\`'s description to match, and added a regression test.

## Test plan
- [x] \`claimVocabulary.test.js\` passes (9/9), including the new test
- [x] \`FILE_TIER_RULE\`'s text matches the actual behavior
